If a Markov chain is irreducible, aperiodic and recurrent,
it has a unique stationary distribution
and the distribution of $\vth^{(t)}$ converges to it
[@gelman2013bda, Section 11.2, p. 279; @robert2004mcsm, Section 6.6.1, Theorem 6.51, p. 234].
Averages along the chain also converge to expectations under that distribution,
even though successive values are correlated
[@robert2004mcsm, Section 6.7.1, Theorem 6.63, p. 241;
@robert2004mcsm, Section 7.2, p. 269].
MCMC algorithms construct a Markov chain
whose stationary distribution is the posterior $\p(\vth \mid \vy)$
[@gelman2013bda, Chapter 11, p. 275],
so that [Monte Carlo estimates](#def-monte-carlo-estimate)
can be computed from the chain's values
in place of independent draws.
